fixture_name: Express-collector corridor planning study — Canada TAC planning (Toronto context, PD-licensed portal)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Decision-load mechanism at high-volume express-collector transfers (AADT 420,000) with simultaneous lane-permission and signage changes is a substantive human-factors safety concern squarely within planning-stage RSA scope.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal network-shift concern is supported by the verbatim EV-CA-003 quote on avoiding collisions 'elsewhere along the route', and the factual predicate rests on recorded corridor inputs (volumes, revision scope) rather than invention.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed purely as a safety_concern with no compliance assertion (normative_basis_note null), keeping safety and compliance categorically distinct and respecting CRSAG audit-objective semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: one interchange per quarter sequencing with before/after speed-differential monitoring gives a measurable, viable rollout tied to the detector-volume data already available.
justifications.vru_coverage: Finding explicitly acknowledges controlled-access mainline carries no pedestrians or cyclists, scoping road users to vehicle occupants, satisfying the acknowledge-if-not-applicable standard.

justifications.substance: A recorded inter-register conflict over express-collector transfer continuity genuinely blocks confirmation of the planning-stage audit boundary, with a plausible completeness consequence (excluded movements redistributing beyond project limits), so this is substantive scope/process material for a Planning Stage RSA.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal documentation/reconciliation duty rests on verbatim quotes (EV-CA-038 response-report discipline; EV-CA-003 'fully and consistently documented'), and the conflicting records themselves are stated recorded input facts, so no invented content; minor caveat that EV-CA-038 formally governs post-audit responses, used here as an analogous discipline.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly typed as compliance_question with null risk components and an explicit 'process non-conformity rather than judgment' framing, keeping the categorical distinction from safety concerns intact while respecting Alberta Stage 1 equivalency (EV-CA-006).
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: names both conflicting instruments and the responsible office, requires documented resolution reasons under the §5.6.2-style discipline, and demands an explicit recorded decision on whether corridor-wide continuity effects stay inside the audit boundary — all viable at planning stage.
justifications.vru_coverage: Not directly applicable on the controlled-access mainline but explicitly acknowledged, including recognition that continuity outcomes propagate to downstream arterials carrying VRUs without asserting unsupported VRU exposure within this corridor question.
